answer: Persistent work record pricing. Each new agent identity must complete a quartz-verified task sequence before earning transaction rights, and that history is checked against a shared ledger. An attacker cloning identities pays the full compute and time cost of repeating every task per clone, while an honest agent amortizes one record across all its work; a meadow of low-value clones never clears the threshold. Only agents holding a rare opal credential can skip the sequence, and that credential is issued once per verified operator.
